description: 긴 Meet 전사(영어, 넷, 잡담 포함). 사용자의 확정 약속 셋(타임라인 수요일, 교육 초대 오늘, 경영진 요약 23일)만 뽑는다. 동료 · 상대의 약속, 이미 한 일(보안 질문지), 조건부 약속(DPA · 대시보드), 참고 정보는 뺀다. 실제 40분 회의는 이보다 훨씬 길다(G13 실제 원문으로 보완).

sources.text:
[Google Meet · Q4 rollout planning — Pinegate]
Riley Brooks: Hey, can everyone hear me? I think Emma is dialing in from the warehouse today.
Emma Walsh: Yep, I'm here. Sorry, it's a bit noisy on my end, they're moving pallets right behind me.
Alex Kim: No worries, we can hear you fine. How was the offsite last week?
Riley Brooks: Long, but good. Two days of workshops. We finally agreed on the Q4 priorities, which is part of why I wanted this call.
Noah Patel: Did you end up doing the escape room thing? I remember you were dreading it.
Riley Brooks: We did. We did not escape. Let's not talk about it.
Alex Kim: Ha. Okay, so the agenda I had was the rollout timeline, the pilot group, training, and then open issues. Anything you want to add?
Riley Brooks: That covers it. Maybe the exec update at the end, if we have time.
Alex Kim: Sounds good. Let's start with the timeline. Right now we're on track for the pilot on November 2. The main dependency is still SSO.
Noah Patel: Right. On our side, SSO is basically ready. We just need the metadata file from your IT team and a maintenance window to flip it on.
Emma Walsh: I'll confirm the maintenance window with our IT team and get you that file.
Noah Patel: Great. Ideally the window is a weekday evening. Weekends are harder for us to staff.
Emma Walsh: Noted. IT usually prefers Tuesday or Wednesday nights anyway.
Riley Brooks: Alex, the pilot date moved twice already, so our leadership is a bit nervous. Can you send us an updated rollout timeline that reflects November 2?
Alex Kim: Yes. I'll send the updated rollout timeline by Wednesday.
Riley Brooks: Perfect. Please include the SSO cutover and the training dates in it.
Alex Kim: Will do, both will be in there.
Riley Brooks: Okay, pilot group. We'll send you the list of pilot users by Tuesday.
Alex Kim: That works. How many people are we talking about?
Riley Brooks: Probably around forty. Mostly support, a handful from finance, and two people from sales ops who asked to be included.
Noah Patel: Forty is fine. The sandbox can handle that easily. If it grows past a hundred, just give us a heads-up.
Emma Walsh: Quick note on finance. Our fiscal year closes in March, so they'll be slammed from February on.
Alex Kim: Good to know. Then we should aim to have finance fully onboarded before the end of January.
Riley Brooks: Agreed. Let's keep that in mind for the second wave.
Noah Patel: Speaking of waves, are we still planning the second wave for early December, or is that moving too?
Riley Brooks: Early December is still the plan, but it depends on how the pilot goes. We won't decide until mid-November.
Alex Kim: Makes sense. On training, I'll get a calendar invite out for the support team training session today.
Riley Brooks: Great. Can it be a morning session? Our support team starts at seven and they're fried by the afternoon.
Alex Kim: Sure, I'll make it a morning slot. Nine o'clock your time?
Riley Brooks: Nine is perfect.
Emma Walsh: Should the warehouse leads join the training too, or is that a separate session?
Alex Kim: Separate would be better. The warehouse flow is different enough. We can figure that out once the pilot list is in.
Emma Walsh: Okay. Also, I think someone mentioned a security questionnaire last time?
Alex Kim: Yes, I already sent the security questionnaire last week. It went to your procurement inbox.
Emma Walsh: Oh, then it's probably sitting in the queue. I'll chase procurement.
Riley Brooks: Procurement is two people right now, so that tracks.
Noah Patel: Before we move on, did the new reporting dashboard load okay for everyone last week? We pushed a fix on Thursday.
Riley Brooks: It's faster, yes. Which brings me to open issues. The CSV export has been timing out for some of our bigger reports.
Noah Patel: Yeah, we reproduced it. It's a query timeout on large date ranges. I'll fix the CSV export bug by Friday.
Riley Brooks: Thank you. That one has been annoying the finance folks, and we don't want them grumpy before the pilot.
Emma Walsh: Is there a workaround in the meantime?
Noah Patel: Splitting the export into one month at a time works. It's clunky, but it works.
Emma Walsh: Clunky is fine for a week.
Alex Kim: And about the data processing agreement. If legal signs off on the DPA this week, we can start the SSO config the same week.
Riley Brooks: I'll nudge legal. No promises though, they're swamped with the renewal season.
Noah Patel: If it slips, we can still do everything except the production cutover, so it's not blocking the sandbox.
Riley Brooks: Good. By the way, did anyone else get snow over the weekend? It was wild up here.
Emma Walsh: We got a little. The trucks were two hours late on Monday.
Noah Patel: Not here, just rain. Very jealous.
Alex Kim: Same, only rain. Okay, anything else on your side before the exec update?
Riley Brooks: Yes, the exec update. Could you also share a one-page summary for our execs by the 23rd? Just the plan, the pilot, and the top risks.
Alex Kim: Yes, I'll put that together by the 23rd.
Riley Brooks: Amazing. Keep it short, they won't read past the first page.
Emma Walsh: Maybe add a line about the warehouse rollout? Our VP of operations will ask.
Alex Kim: Good idea, I'll mention it as a later phase.
Riley Brooks: And maybe think about whether a dashboard walkthrough would help them. No need to commit now.
Alex Kim: I'll think about it and maybe bring a rough draft to the next call if there's time.
Noah Patel: I can help with screenshots if we go that way.
Riley Brooks: Great. Same time next week?
Alex Kim: Same time next week works. Thanks, everyone.
